description: Write one instruction in each sentence and keep procedural sentences to 20 words or fewer.

questions.prompt: Which step obeys the STE rule of one instruction per sentence?
options: Remove the cover and disconnect the cable, then install the new filter.
Remove the cover and put it on the bench.
questions.explanation: Write only one instruction in each sentence. A reader who does one action at a time makes fewer mistakes.

questions.prompt: When can a procedural sentence contain two instructions?
options: When the reader does the two actions at the same time.
When the second instruction is optional.
questions.explanation: Two instructions are permitted in one sentence only when the reader does them at the same time, for example 'Push and hold the TEST button.'

questions.prompt: Write the first step of: 'Disconnect the battery and then remove the cover.'
questions.explanation: Split the sentence into two steps: 'Disconnect the battery.' Then: 'Remove the cover.'

questions.prompt: Tap the words that join a second instruction to this step:
questions.sentence: Close the valve and then stop the pump.
questions.approvedAlternative: Close the valve. Stop the pump.
questions.explanation: 'And then' joins two actions that the reader does one after the other. Write them as two steps.

questions.prompt: What is the maximum length of an STE procedural sentence?
questions.explanation: Procedural sentences have a maximum of 20 words. Descriptive sentences can have up to 25 words.

questions.prompt: This text has three instructions. Write only the first one, in 20 words or fewer. Keep 'make sure', 'power' and 'off':
questions.initialText: Make sure that the electrical power is off and then carefully disconnect the cable from the connector on the rear panel and put a cap on the connector to keep out dust.
questions.explanation: Give each instruction its own sentence: 'Make sure that the electrical power is off.' Then 'Disconnect the cable from the rear connector.' Then 'Put a cap on the connector.'
